title: "Hands-On: Submodule and Worktree"
---

# Hands-On: A Repo with a Submodule and a Worktree

Two small Git repos on Linux, then a worktree of the parent.

## Child library

```bash
mkdir -p ~/desk/desk-lib
cd ~/desk/desk-lib
git init
echo "DESK_LIB=1" > version.txt
git add version.txt
git commit -m "chore: desk-lib version pin"
```

## Parent with submodule

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git submodule add ~/desk/desk-lib src/desk-lib
git status
git commit -m "chore: add desk-lib submodule"
ls src/desk-lib/version.txt
```

## Worktree of the parent

```bash
git worktree add ~/desk/desk-api-wt -b feat/wt-lab
cd ~/desk/desk-api-wt
git status
echo "worktree lab" >> README.md
git add README.md
git commit -m "docs: worktree lab"
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git log --oneline feat/wt-lab -1
```

`main` in `~/desk/desk-api` does not have that commit until you merge.

## Cleanup

```bash
cd ~/desk/desk-api
git worktree remove ~/desk/desk-api-wt
git switch main
git merge --ff-only feat/wt-lab
git branch -d feat/wt-lab
```

Leave the submodule in place for later chapters, or remove it:

```bash
git rm src/desk-lib
git commit -m "chore: remove desk-lib submodule"
rm -rf ~/desk/desk-lib
```

Removing the submodule does not delete `~/desk/desk-lib` unless you `rm -rf` it.

## Done when

- `git worktree list` shows only the main tree
- You know whether `src/desk-lib` is still a gitlink (`git ls-files -s src/desk-lib` shows mode `160000`) or is gone

Next: Git Flow, GitHub Flow, trunk-based — how teams name these branches on purpose.
